newsitem.title: USA: MCI asks court to overturn FCC access-charge rule.
newsitem.headline: MCI asks court to overturn FCC access-charge rule.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp has asked a U.S. appeals court to overturn a federal overhaul of domestic phone charges, saying the rules do not go far enough to cut the charges long-distance carriers pay to access the local phone network, MCI officials said Tuesday.
The No. 2 long-distance carrier filed the suit against the Federal Communications Commission rules in a court in Washington DC.

The FCC last month ordered a $1.7 billion reduction in the $23 billion in annual charges that long-distance carriers pay local companies to access their networks. The cut is supposed to take effect July 1.
The FCC also ordered an $18.5 billion reduction in access charges over the next years.
MCI had wanted the FCC to order an upfront reduction of some $10 billion.
MCI apparently is the first carrier to ask the courts to overturn the FCC rules -- although more challenges are likely.
SBC Communications Inc recenty asked the FCC to suspend the rules -- saying the access-charge reductions went too far.
The FCC is expected to turn down the request, which is likely to prompt SBC to ask the court to order the agency to make changes.

Analyst Dwight Allen of Deloitte & Touche Consulting Group said the MCI suit reflects the potential side-effects of Congress's decision to leave vague key aspects of last year's big communications law.

"This is an example of where they did not try to prescribe anything about access charges," Allen said. "In the American system, this is how we arrive at policy," he added, referring to regulators issuing rules which are then challenged in court.
"Congress wanted to take back telecommunications policy from the courts," he noted wryly.
